bio: Dr. Oh joined the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee in 2016. Her research focuses on improving health and quality of life through technology-supported self-management and family management interventions. She studies family management among individuals with autism, developing communication support technologies that promote social participation and independence while reducing caregiver burden. She also develops and evaluates technology-based interventions for adults with metabolic chronic conditions, including cardiovascular disease, diabetes, obesity, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia, using artificial intelligence, mobile health, voice assistants, and natural language processing to improve modifiable risk factors, health behaviors, and self-management outcomes. Her contributions include developing the Cardiac Health Behavior Scale for Adults with Cardiovascular Risks or Diseases (CHB-K21) and validating nursing-sensitive self-management outcomes across multiple chronic conditions. 1st Place PhD Poster Award, Sigma (Eta Nu Chapter), 11th Annual Poster Symposium, University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee School of Nursing, 2025. research_summary: Robotic-Assisted Stroke Rehabilitation Aging Research and Machine Learning – Applying predictive modeling to analyze aging trends, establish normative data, detect biomarkers, and identify risk factors across the lifespan Rehabilitation Outcome Measures – Developing the iNeck risk assessment model for tech neck and neck pain prevention (TNNP) Biomarkers of Aging and Frailty – Constructing a frailty index and identifying aging biomarkers using electronic health records (EHRs). Inga Wang (former Ying-Chih Wang), Ph.D., OTR/L, is a Professor with School of Rehabilitation Sciences & Technology. Her research is centered around two primary areas: (1) Robotic-Assisted Stroke Rehabilitation, (2) Aging Research and Machine Learning. In the past, Dr. Wang has assisted Dr. Craig Velozo in various outcome research projects, focusing on computerized adaptive testing (CAT) and score equating, funded by the National Institute on Disability and Rehabilitation Research (NIDRR) and VA Rehabilitation Research and Development (RR&D). She has also assisted Dr. Zev Rymer, Vice President for Research at the RIC, on NIH-funded projects, including the Toolbox project. This project aims to provide investigators with a brief yet comprehensive measurement tool for assessing cognitive, emotional, sensory, and motor function in large cohort studies such as epidemiological studies, clinical trials, or clinical studies, as part of the NIH Blueprint for Neuroscience. Over the years, she has published population-based reference values for motor performance measurements, including grip strength, dexterity, balance functions, and aging biomarkers across the lifespan. With her background in neurorehabilitation and fellowship training in rehabilitation technology, Dr. Wang collaborates with engineers to assess the user experience and efficacy of upper limb robotic-assisted therapy for individuals with neurological disorders. In 2009, Dr. Wang was funded by a 5-yr NIDRR training center grant as a PI on Sub-Project on enhancing the functional and employment outcomes of individuals who experience a Stroke. Since 2021, Dr. Wang has been involved in NIDILRR's Disability and Rehabilitation Research Projects, focusing on studying the feasibility and usability of SREx, iTbot, mR2A and other rehabilitation robotics in rehabilitation of the paretic arm, particularly in stroke survivors. The integration of these robotics with Azure app, Digital Twin, and HoloLens aims to enable therapists to interact with patients and control the devices remotely. The ultimate goal is to design high-functioning robotic devices for routine clinical neurorehabilitation and cost-effective options for home-based robot-assisted telerehabilitation.

bio: I pride myself on establishing a meaningful relationship with all patients I care for. As an interventional endoscopist, I often see patients that are referred from other gastroenterologists and physicians for complex endoscopic problems. This occasionally results in meeting the patient for the first time right before his/her procedure. I make every effort to explain the problem, and the treatment plan to the patient and his/her loved one(s) so that they understand what we propose to do and what the next steps will be. Additionally, I place a high value on multidisciplinary care and collaboration. Many patients I treat are also cared for by other specialists and in these circumstances, input from the entire treatment team is imperative to optimize patient outcomes. Further, some conditions such as pancreatic fluid collections have various treatment options that span disciplines such as hepato-pancreaticobiliary surgery and interventional radiology. Only when we discuss and plan treatment strategies in a collaborative manner, are we able to achieve the best outcomes for our patients. Dr. Smith did his gastroenterology and hepatology training at the Medical College of Wisconsin. awards.title: Enlisting HPV integration events to illuminate drivers and target treatment in invasive cervical cancer
awards.abstract: PROJECT SUMMARY Invasive cervical cancer (ICC) kills nearly 311,000 women each year worldwide with an estimated 50% increase in deaths by 2040. In the U.S., ICC ranks third for average years of life lost. Women with advanced or recurrent ICC soon develop resistance to current chemotherapy options, and about 90% die within 2 years. Our intent is to define clinically relevant and targetable ICC genes and pathways to improve patients’ treatments and outcomes. Our central hypothesis is that HPV integration events—and the changes they exert on the host genome and epigenome—confer a selective advantage to disease progression and provide opportunities to pinpoint genes and pathways relevant to treating ICC. awards.abstract: PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT Integration of the human papillomavirus (HPV) into the host genome is a dominant feature of invasive cervical cancer (ICC). Genomic coordinates of integration sites have been identified in many tumors, but little is known about the nature of the cis genomic changes at these sites or how they might promote ICC. Harnessing data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) along with patient-matched long-read sequencing of HPV integration sites will define novel genes/pathways affecting ICC outcome. Aim 1 will define HPV integration sites in the TCGA- MCW cervical cancer cohort using newly developed HPV DNA capture for long-read sequencing. bio: Dr. Janet S. Rader became the Jack A. & Elaine D. Klieger Professor and Chair of the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology at the Medical College of Wisconsin in 2009. She earned her medical degree from the University of Missouri, completed residency training at Michael Reese Hospital and Medical Center, and a gynecologic oncology fellowship at Johns Hopkins Hospital. She is board certified in Obstetrics and Gynecology and Gynecologic Oncology. A physician-scientist, Dr. Rader’s career spans more than three decades of clinical care, research, team science, and workforce development. Her practice focuses on the management of gynecologic cancers. Recognized among the nation’s leading gynecologic oncologists, she has been named to U.S. News & World Report’s Top Doctors list and is ranked among the top physicians in her specialty nationwide. Supported by the NIH, ACS, and other national funding agencies, Dr. Rader’s research focuses on the molecular drivers of gynecologic cancers and their translation into new treatment strategies. She has led investigator-initiated and cooperative group clinical trials incorporating translational research endpoints. A nationally recognized leader in collaborative science, Dr. Rader served on the steering committee for The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) Ovarian Pilot Project and co-chaired the TCGA Cervical Cancer Disease Working Group. name: Danny Thomas
title: Professor of Pediatrics
directory_research: Data-driven pediatric concussion research to improve outcomes and care
research_summary: Dr. Thomas’ primary research goal is to improve identification of concussion and early management in the acute care setting. He has been interested in brain injury since studying psychology as an undergraduate. His initial research developed objective ways to assess concussion severity in the ED. Dr. Thomas has looked at factors that influence recovery from concussion to improve our understanding of the role of rest, exercise, and recovery from concussion. He published a randomized trial of strict rest after acute concussion which was covered widely by major national media outlets. These findings have challenged the existing understanding of the “benefits” of rest and the “harm” of activity post concussion. Currently Dr. Thomas is looking for ways to improve and speed initial recover, decrease risk of subsequent injury, and identify patients at higher risk for post-concussive syndrome.

awards.abstract: PROJECT SUMMARY Concussion impacts nearly 2 million children each year. Up to 30% of these patients will experience symptoms lasting weeks to months after injury. Current practice recommends strict rest for 24-48 hours post-concussion followed by a symptom-guided return to activity. Emerging evidence shows prolonged rest may be harmful by contributing to deconditioning, impeding the brain's nascent ability to heal, and/or setting up psychological barriers to recovery. We recently published results from a randomized controlled trial (RCT) of strict rest following acute concussion and found patients who were prescribed prolonged rest experienced greater symptoms and slower recovery. bio: Dr. Sara Sabbagh is an associate professor of pediatrics in the division of rheumatology at the Medical College of Wisconsin and Children's Wisconsin. She is a physician-scientist specializing in juvenile dermatomyositis (JDM) and other idiopathic inflammatory myopathies affecting children. Dr. Sabbagh's research focuses on understanding the mechanisms of vasculopathy – blood vessel dysfunction – in juvenile dermatomyositis. Her long-term goal is to translate these discoveries into novel targeted therapies that improve outcomes for children with this rare autoimmune disease. Her work investigates how immune cells, particularly macrophages and regulatory T cells, interact with blood vessel cells to drive inflammation and tissue damage in JDM. As a clinician, Dr. Sabbagh brings extensive expertise in caring for children with inflammatory myopathies. She completed her pediatric rheumatology fellowship at Children's National Medical Center and National Institutes of Health (NIH/NIAMS). Following fellowship, she received specialized clinical training in myositis assessments under internationally recognized experts in myositis at the NIH. Dr. Sabbagh is deeply committed to collaborative research and improving care for children with JDM. bio: Dr. Kimberly Gecsi joined the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology in August 2021 in the Division of General Obstetrics and Gynecology. Dr. Gecsi received her medical degree from Case Western Reserve University School of Medicine in Cleveland, Ohio in 2002. She went on to complete her residency in Obstetrics and Gynecology at the University of Pittsburgh Magee Womens Hospital from 2002 to 2006. Prior to starting at the Medical College of Wisconsin, Dr. Gecsi spent 12 years in academic medicine in Cleveland where she held leadership roles including residency program director. She is an active member of several national organizations and is on the board of directors for the Society of Academic Specialists in General Obstetrics and Gynecology. Dr. Gecsi’s clinical passion is minimally invasive gynecologic surgery, which encompasses hysteroscopy, laparoscopy, and robotic-assisted laparoscopy. These techniques allow safe and complete treatment of gynecologic conditions including abnormal uterine bleeding, uterine fibroids, endometrial polyps, adenomyosis, and endometriosis, while allowing for less time in the hospital and quicker return to work and activities. She also specializes in lower genital tract pathology including cervical dysplasia and vulvar disorders. I believe every patient should have access to high quality, patient centered care. awards.abstract: ABSTRACT Infection with human Cytomegalovirus (HCMV) is nearly universal; seroprevalence rates reach 90% in individuals older than 80. Although usually asymptomatic in the normal host, HCMV causes severe morbidity and mortality in transplant recipients and patients with AIDS. Congenital HCMV is the leading infectious cause of childhood deafness and mental retardation. There is no approved vaccine for the prevention of HCMV. The nucleoside analog ganciclovir (GCV) and its oral formulation val-GCV have improved the outcome of transplantation. GCV may also prevent hearing deterioration in congenitally infected children. However, prolonged courses of GCV or val-GCV result in intolerable toxicities to the bone marrow and select for resistant viral strains. awards.abstract: Crohn's disease (CD) is a multifactorial and complex disease, orchestrated by several genetic and environmental triggers. The best known genetic marker for CD is the nucleotide oligomerization domain 2 (NOD2), a cytoplasmic receptor that responds to bacterial pathogens. Mutations in NOD2 are the strongest genetic marker for CD and the only proven risk factor for stricturing phenotypes. The fact that mutations in NOD2 result in CD only in some individuals but not in others indicates that environmental factors may contribute to or trigger CD. CMV, a common viral infection, establishes life-long latency in the host including in intestinal epithelial cells. Our laboratory reported that NOD2 suppresses CMV replication, but the NOD2 mutant 3020insC, associated with severe CD, is unable to inhibit CMV replication in vitro. awards.abstract: PROJECT SUMMARY Preterm infants are born with immature lungs and immature neural control of breathing. They rely on supplemental oxygen therapy (hyperoxia; HX). Though necessary for survival, they require HX which progressively damages the lungs and causes bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD), the most common respiratory complication among preterm infants. bio: Dr. Mouradian received his BA from Carthage College in Kenosha, Wisconsin in 2009. In 2014 he obtained his PhD in Physiology from the Medical College of Wisconsin. His PhD work was focused on understanding the role of peripheral carotid body O2 chemosensors and their role in 1) maintaining eupneic breathing and 2) gain modulation of the central CO2 chemosensors. He used a combination of whole-animal physiology and RNA Sequencing. He then completed four years of postdoctoral training at the University of Colorado in Denver and MCW, where he studied the role of oxidative stress in lung diseases (pulmonary hypertension, idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, and bronchopulmonary dysplasia). He synthesized his passion and interests in neural control of breathing with lung biology to garner the prestigious Parker B. Francis Award. This award paved the way for a faculty position which led to the start of his independent laboratory in February of 2022 where he directs research focusing on how lung disease impacts the neural control of breathing via damage to vagal fibers that innervate the lung. Dr. Mouradian is a proponent of assisting his lab members define and reach their own career goals. directory_research: AI-driven simulation methods to uncover mechanisms of membrane transport
research_summary: s how cells function at the molecular level, with a focus on membrane transport, signaling, and morphological changes. This research relies on state-of-the-art and advanced molecular simulation techniques, grounded in statistical mechanics and machine learning. A core aspect of our research is the development of novel methodologies to integrate molecular simulations with diverse experimental data sources, such as NMR, EPR, FRET, cryo-EM, and HDX-MS. Our team also pioneers enhanced sampling methods and new approaches for rationalizing simulation and experimental data. This highly interdisciplinary work often involves close collaboration with leading experimental labs. By bridging structure and dynamics, our research aims to advance our understanding of proteins and cellular membranes across both molecular and supramolecular scales, with the goal of discovering new therapies for diseases, particularly in the areas of infectious diseases, drug resistance, and cancer. Lab Members William Brown, PhD, Postdoctoral Researcher Sandra Byju, PhD, Postdoctoral Researcher Mrina Mtenga, ACS Post Baccalaureate Fellow Nirjala Patel, Undergraduate Student Tyler Trask, Graduate Student Research Highlight Title: Multi-Ensemble Reweighting Enables Structural Interpretation of Differential HDX-MS Authors: Sandra Byju, Vincent Lowe, Daniel Deredge, Fabrizio Marinelli Brief description: The manuscript introduces multi-state HDX ensemble reweighting, a new method for integrative structural modeling that addresses a longstanding challenge in differential hydrogen–deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS): deuterium loss, which can account for 10–50% of the signal. The method extends applicability from approximately one-quarter to the vast majority of HDX-MS datasets while improving structural accuracy. Applications to distinct protein systems demonstrate its versatility for detecting alternative structural states and quantifying population shifts using both molecular dynamics simulations and AI-predicted ensembles, including those generated by AlphaFold3 and AFsample3. Read the full preprint on BioRxiv .
bio: I earned my PhD in statistical and biological physics from the International School for Advanced Studies in Trieste, Italy, where I developed innovative molecular simulation techniques to explore protein structure, dynamics, and function. My postdoctoral work at the Max Planck Institute of Biophysics in Frankfurt, Germany, and later at the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI) of the National Institutes of Health (NIH), focused on advancing computational methods to study transport across biological membranes. In 2016, I was appointed staff scientist at NHLBI/NIH, where I led an interdisciplinary research program aimed at understanding the mechanisms of key membrane transport proteins and developing computational approaches to integrate simulations with experimental data, such as EPR/DEER and HDX-MS. During my time at the NIH, I was also actively involved in teaching and mentoring. In July 2024, I joined the Medical College of Wisconsin as assistant professor of biophysics and data science, and have been approved for promotion to associate professor effective July 2025. I also hold an adjunct senior investigator position at the Versiti Blood Research Institute. My current research at MCW focuses on developing computational models to tackle key biological and medical problems.

name: Michael Martens
title: Assistant Professor
directory_research: Clinical trials, survival analysis, machine learning, data monitoring, Bayesian methods
research_summary: Adaptive Trial Design Bayesian Statistics Blood and Marrow Transplant Research Clinical Trial Machine Learning Observational Study Oncology Survival Analysis Variable Selection Clinical trials are conducted to evaluate the potential benefit of proposed therapies. Because these studies can incur tremendous costs and require multiple years to conduct, statistical techniques that can reduce the expense and duration hold great value, including group sequential testing, adaptive design, and covariate adjustment. Time to event outcomes are often the primary interest in these trials, particularly in oncology; but these endpoints, in comparison to binary or continuous ones, require increasingly complex methodology in order to incorporate these techniques. In addition, accurate sample size calculation is crucial for both clinical trials and observations studies to permit them to meet their objectives while avoiding wasting resources. My research goals include providing innovative group sequential tests and adaptive design methods for time to event endpoints in clinical trials, improving the precision of treatment evaluation and flexibility of the study as well as and reducing patient burden and study duration. Furthermore, I am interested in developing a general framework for accurate sample size calculation applicable to a wide variety of regression models and studies that accounts for any correlation among covariates and between subjects. These aims for future research are inspired by my experiences as a senior biostatistician at The Emmes Company (Emmes), providing statistical guidance and support for clinical trials research in blood and marrow transplant, cellular therapies, and ophthalmology. My previous work in statistical methodology includes group sequential testing of time to event outcomes, sample size determination for generalized linear models and time to event regression models, and nonparametric Bayesian inference. bio: Clinical trials are conducted to evaluate the potential benefit of proposed therapies. Because these studies can incur tremendous costs and require multiple years to conduct, statistical techniques that can reduce the expense and duration hold great value, including group sequential testing, adaptive design, and covariate adjustment. Time to event outcomes are often the primary interest in these trials, particularly in oncology; but these endpoints, in comparison to binary or continuous ones, require increasingly complex methodology in order to incorporate these techniques. In addition, accurate sample size calculation is crucial for both clinical trials and observations studies to permit them to meet their objectives while avoiding wasting resources. My research goals include providing innovative group sequential tests and adaptive design methods for time to event endpoints in clinical trials, improving the precision of treatment evaluation and flexibility of the study as well as and reducing patient burden and study duration. Furthermore, I am interested in developing a general framework for accurate sample size calculation applicable to a wide variety of regression models and studies that accounts for any correlation among covariates and between subjects. Conceptual understanding is developed through thinking about mathematical ideas, how these ideas are interrelated, and how they can be applied in various real-life situations. In her courses, she spends a significant amount of time in discussions related to key examples that focus on understanding the meaning of the mathematical concepts capitalizing on a student's prior knowledge and preparing them for future learning.

He joined the faculty in 2019. Before joining academia, he worked as a lead quality assurance engineer for MERGE Healthcare.

He also consults on helping companies adhere to government regulations as well as safe work practices.

Dr. Carl also has industry consulting experience at Digital Design Corporation/Advanced Network Devices and at Johnson Controls.

bio: Dr. Victoria Carlson-Oehlers is an associate professor in the MSOE School of Nursing and is involved with the Medical Brigade of MSOE's chapter of Global Brigades. Most of her career was devoted to pediatric care, but in recent years, Carlson-Oehlers has shifted her research focus to short-term humanitarian experiences. She spoke in Jerusalem about teaching students in a humanitarian awareness culture and teaches a class that prepares students to travel to Central America.

bio: Dr. Michael Carriere is a professor in MSOE’s Humanities, Social Science and Communication Department. He also is director of the Honors Program. He is an urban historian and studies the growth and evolution of communities and the impact of social issues. He works closely with MSOE's honors students on ‘real-world’ projects that allow young engineers to develop their respective skill sets while practicing a pedagogy based on collaboration, interdisciplinary and inter-institutional partnerships. Carriere spent two years as a junior fellow at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, a Washington D.C. think tank, before entering graduate school at the University of Chicago and earning a Ph.D. in American history.

He is a Registered Professional Engineer in the State of Wisconsin and his areas of specialization are communication systems, satellite communications, spread spectrum, telecommunications and networking, and control systems. He continues to consult for clients in industry and government.

bio: Chaucey Chandler is an accomplished, innovative operations and program leader with an extensive record of successfully incorporating productivity improvements into transactional & manufacturing processes to increase efficiency and improve production while overseeing change management.

bio: Dr. Yu-Sin Chang joined the Mathematics Department as an Assistant Professor in Fall 2018. She earned her Ph.D. in Applied Mathematics from Illinois Institute of Technology. Her research focuses on the areas of Probability, Stochastics, and Financial Mathematics. Dr. Chang worked in financial industry as a Quantitative Researcher for two and half years and has the Financial Risk Manager (FRM) designation. Dr. Chang received the Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics Early Career Award in 2019. She contributes to the Actuarial Science program and general mathematical courses.

bio: Dr. Lesya Chorna is an adjunct assistant professor in the Mathematics Department at MSOE. bio: Rachel Christopherson is a clinical assistant professor in the M.S. Perfusion program in the (ECBE) Electrical, Computer and Biomedical Engineering department. She has been a faculty member at MSOE since 2025. Rachel graduated from MSOE’s Master of Science in Perfusion program in March 2024 and joined the team at Advocate Aurora Medical Group in April 2024 where she is currently a staff perfusionist. As a clinical instructor, she shares her passion and knowledge of perfusion to foster the education and success of students.

bio: Andrew Chromy is currently working as the Chief Business and Finance Officer for the Oak Creek-Franklin Joint School District. He is also an adjunct professor at MSOE and teaching courses in the MBA program related to Intro to Finance and coursework for school business management.

DuPont De Nemours in Wilmington, Del.; a research chemist in the Chemical Process Section of Exxon Production Research Co. in Houston; as new product development manager/radiation safety officer for CERAC Inc. in Milwaukee; and as principal/owner of MCC Research Enterprises LLC in Glendale, Wis.

He has been a faculty member at MSOE since 2015. He is the perfusion supervisor for Children's Wisconsin, and previously worked as a staff perfusionist for Children's Wisconsin and Medical College of Wisconsin.

bio: Dr. Christopher Damm has served on the faculty of the Mechanical Engineering Department at MSOE for over 15 years. He teaches courses in thermodynamics, heat transfer, fluid mechanics, engineering design and advanced energy technologies. He is an expert in the areas of renewable energy and emerging energy systems (solar, wind, combined heat and power); air pollution control; and forensic engineering/safety in engineering design. He has also worked to decrease air pollution from the transportation sector.

bio: Dr. Mitzi Dobersek, P.E., is an expert in transportation engineering with an emphasis on traffic signal design and operation, traffic operations, traffic analysis, and intersection design. She has over 30 years of experience with the Wisconsin Department of Transportation in various roles including traffic operations supervisor, signal operations engineer, and traffic engineer. Dr. Dobersek is an associate professor in the Civil and Architectural Engineering and Construction Management Department at MSOE.

name: Alicia Domack
title: Department Chair, Professor
research_summary: Learning and Development; Educational Psychology; Cognition
bio: Dr. Alicia Domack is a professor and chair of the Humanities, Social Science and Communication Department at MSOE. Originally from Omaha, Nebraska, she received her bachelor's degree in psychology from the University of Wisconsin, Madison. She received her master's degree in school psychology from the University of Nebraska, Omaha and her doctorate in educational psychology, with a specialization in cognition, learning and development, from the University of Nebraska, Lincoln. Dr. Domack joined MSOE in 2009 and was drawn to MSOE by the caliber of students, the urban environment and the exciting opportunities for collaboration. Her research interests range from the science of teaching and learning to the psychology of place. During her tenure as HSC department chair, she has worked with faculty to launch the UX program, support new minors in psychology and Spanish, expand the University Scholars Honors program, and led multiple committees and task force groups associated with MSOE's Strategic Plan. She has served as MSOE's HLC accreditation liasion officer, and IRB Director. In 2017, Dr. Domack was awarded Milwaukee Business Journal's 40 Under 40 award.

bio: Dr. Icaro dos Santos is an Associate Professor in the Electrical, Computer and Biomedical Engineering department and has been a faculty member at MSOE since 2016. Dr. Ícaro dos Santos is an accomplished biomedical engineer and academic with extensive experience in medical device innovation and strategic business planning. He holds a Ph.D. in Electrical and Computer Engineering from the University of Texas at Austin, where he specialized in cardiac ablation, and an MBA in Strategy from the University of Wisconsin. Currently, Dr. dos Santos serves as an Associate Professor at the Milwaukee School of Engineering, where he develops curriculum and laboratory materials for Biomedical Engineering courses. He is also the Manager at VIKARE, leading the design and development of medical devices for CO2 management. With a robust background in both academia and industry, Dr. dos Santos has held key positions such as Principal Research and Development Engineer at ComfortApnea and Chief Research Officer at Astus Medical Manufacturing. His work has led to several patents, including innovations in sleep apnea therapy and negative air pressure devices. Dr. dos Santos is fluent in English and Portuguese and has a proven track record in obtaining FDA approvals, developing prototypes, and securing research grants. His contributions to the field are further evidenced by numerous journal and conference publications, as well as his leadership in various industry-funded projects. In addition to his

She has been a faculty member at MSOE since 2026. She is an experienced cardiovascular perfusionist with more than 12 years of adult clinical practice with a comprehensive background of cardiac, vascular, and oncological perfusion practices. Draths prioritizes a safe, efficient and collaborative approach to providing perfusion services to ensure optimal patient outcomes and is BLS Certified.

name: Margaret Dwyer

bio: Margaret Dwyer is an instructor in the Humanities, Social Science, and Communication Department at MSOE. She earned her bachelor's degree in history and English from Marquette University, her master's degree in U.S. history from the University of Wisconsin-Madison, and her teaching certificate from the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee. She joined MSOE in 2007. Dwyer teaches Freshman Studies I, Freshman Studies II, Freshman Studies III, United States History I, and Creative Thinking. She has industry experience serving as a publications editor for the Wisconsin Department of Public Instruction and the State Historical Society of Wisconsin.

bio: Richard Dykowski is an instructor in the Mechanical Engineering Department at MSOE. His specialties include new product development, powertrain design and development, vibration/dynamics, system integration and metal fatigue. He earned his bachelor’s and master’s degrees in mechanical engineering from the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign. He eared his law degree from Marquette University Law School.

name: Jeremy Edison
title: Assistant Professor
research_summary: Mathematics Anxiety; Representation Theory; Abstract Algebra; Linear Algebra; Mathematics Education; Operator Algebras; Theory of Rings and Associative Algebras
research_tags: theory of rings and associative algebras
bio: Jeremy Edison, Ph.D., is an assistant professor in the Mathematics Department at Milwaukee School of Engineering. He teaches undergraduate mathematics, including calculus and discrete mathematics, and conducts research in algebra and linear algebra. His scholarly work examines invertible algebras, Ore extensions and triangularization of operator algebras on infinite-dimensional vector spaces. His research has appeared in the Journal of Algebra and has included collaborations with Miodrag C. Iovanov and Alexander Sistko. Edison also has experience in mathematics education and interdisciplinary academic initiatives. Before joining Milwaukee School of Engineering, he served in mathematics faculty and leadership roles at Mount Mary University, where his work included mathematical instruction, faculty collaboration and initiatives addressing math anxiety. He earned a Bachelor of Arts from Knox College and a Master of Science and Ph.D. from the University of Iowa.

She also serves as the director of performance excellence at ProHealth Care where she is responsible for measurement and monitoring and performance improvement for the health system. She is ASQ Certified Six Sigma Black Belt and is Lean Certified.

bio: Dr. Jennifer Farrell is an associate professor in the Humanities, Social Science and Communication Department at MSOE. She earned her bachelor's degree in English-creative writing from the University of Montana, her master's in English from Montana State University, and her doctorate in English from Louisiana State University. She has extensive teaching experience at universities and colleges in Montana and Louisiana. Farrell joined MSOE in 2008. She teaches Freshmen Studies I, Freshman Studies III, Science Fiction, American Culture, and literature classes ranging from Literature of the Developing World, to Classics in Literature, to Fantasy Literature..

bio: Bill Farrow is an Associate Professor in MSOE’s Mechanical Engineering Department. He first worked at MSOE as a part-time lecturer from 1992-95 while earning his doctorate in mechanical engineering at Marquette University. Prior to returning to MSOE in 2001, he worked as a research scientist at the Eaton Corporation. His teaching and research interests lie in the field of mechanical engineering.

name: Brian Faulkner
title: Associate Professor
bio: Dr. Brian Faulkner is an Associate Professor in the Electrical, Computer and Biomedical Engineering department and has been a faculty member at MSOE since 2019. He teaches courses in digital signal processing, linear circuits, signals and systems, and electrical engineering.

name: Larry Fennigkoh
title: Professor Emeritus
research_summary: Biomedical Engineering; Medical Devices; Clinical Engineering; Medical Imaging
bio: Dr. Larry Fennigkoh is a Professor Emeritus in the Electrical, Computer and Biomedical Engineering department and has been a faculty member at MSOE since 1983. He specializes in forensic engineering, control of medical error, medical device-related injuries and deaths, and human factors in medical instrumentation design. Previously, Fennigkoh served as the director of clinical engineering at St. Luke’s Medical Center in Milwaukee. He also developed an algorithm to help hospitals determine how much and how often medical devices need to be inspected for maintenance. The algorithm was adopted by the federal regulatory agency and is still used today by hospitals around the world. In addition, Fennigkoh continues to do forensic engineering consulting work on medical device-related patient injuries and deaths—cases which he is often able to tie back to his classroom lectures.

name: Brittany Finger

bio: Brittany Finger is a clinical assistant professor in the M.S. Perfusion program in the (ECBE) Electrical, Computer and Biomedical Engineering department. She has been a faculty member at MSOE since 2022. Brittany has been a full time practicing perfusionist since 2014; working with both adult and pediatric patient populations. She is a Master TeamSTEPPS trainer and works to encourage safe culture within hospital teams.

He also spent time as an attorney, practicing in the areas of intellectual property and estate planning.

bio: Adam Friedman is a lecturer in MSOE's Civil and Architectural Engineering and Construction Management Department. He is a senior associate at CSD Structural Engineers located in Milwaukee, WI. His background includes the structural design and analysis of heavy industrial buildings, commercial structures, connection design, and miscellaneous steel, specifically, stairs and rails. Adam has additional design experience related to construction engineering projects including temporary bracing, erection planning, rigging design, heavy lift planning, hurricane contingency plans, and field modifications.

name: Matthew Frise
title: Associate Professor
research_summary: Technology Ethics; Business Ethics; Ancient Greek Philosophy; Philosophy of Mind; Epistemology; Philosophy of Religion; Biomedical Ethics; Logic
bio: Dr. Matthew Frise is an assistant professor of philosophy at Milwaukee School of Engineering. His scholarly work focuses on memory as it pops up in epistemology, cognitive psychology, and the philosophy of mind. He is also interested in philosophy of religion. Frise was a lecturer at Santa Clara University, a Postdoctoral Research Fellow at Baylor University and a Dissertation Fellow at Saint Louis University. He received his Ph.D. in philosophy from the University of Rochester in May 2015. Frise's research has been published in such journals as Philosophy and Phenomenological Research, Philosophical Studies, The Philosophical Quarterly, Synthese, American Philosophical Quarterly, Pacific Philosophical Quarterly, and Erkenntnis.

bio: Dr. Kseniya Fuhrman is a professor and Chair of the Mathematics Department at MSOE, where she joined the faculty in 2006. She teaches a variety of courses to students of all majors, as well as courses for the actuarial science program.

name: Lucas Garcia
title: Lecturer
research_summary: Hydraulics; HMIs; Software Development; PLCS; Machine Learning
bio: As an Advanced Technologies Engineer at Milwaukee School of Engineering (MSOE), Lucas Garcia leads a group of researchers and engineers who integrate cutting-edge technologies into fluid power projects for industry customers, academic partners, and internal initiatives. He has over 10 years of experience in the automation and testing field, with a master's degree in engineering and a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering from MSOE and Fachhochschule Lübeck in Germany. Lucas' core competencies include designing, building, commissioning, and maintaining electronically controlled hydraulic test stands, providing automated controls and data analysis solutions, and managing projects and people within budget and time constraints. He also has strong communication and leadership skills, developed through training dealers and internal employees on the latest technology, troubleshooting quality issues in the field, and collaborating with end users directly. Lucas' mission is to apply his technical and business skills to advance the state of the art in fluid power and related fields, and to empower his team and organization to achieve excellence and innovation.

name: Robin Gates
title: Assistant Professor
research_summary: Nursing; Healthcare; Hospitals
bio: Robin Gates is a nurse executive with a wide range of experience in community home, health and hospice, organ and tissue donation, managing primary care clinics, and clinical trials involving medical devices and pharmaceuticals. She has also worked as a nurse educator for health care organizations and higher education.

name: Patrick Gathof, JR

bio: Patrick Gathof is an ambitious Industrial Engineer and Leader with strong passion around continuous learning, personal development, and process improvement. He has 5+ years of industrial engineering experience in a manufacturing environment, along with 2+ years of professional leadership experience. Patrick is currently an Operations Project Leader at J.W. Speaker Corporation. He is a board member for the Wisconsin IISE chapter, as well as a member on the IISE Industry Advisory Board. He is currently pursuing my MBA from UW Whitewater, with an emphasis in Data Analytics.

bio: Dr. Chris GauthierDickey is the inaugural Head of the Dwight and Dian Diercks School of Advanced Computing and the Direct Supply Chair of Applied AI and Software Innovation. GauthierDickey brings a distinguished record of academic leadership, research innovation, and a deep commitment to excellence in computing education. In this role, GauthierDickey leads the school’s strategic initiatives, including expanding applied AI education, strengthening industry partnerships and enhancing experiential learning opportunities. He also oversees the continued development of MSOE’s high-performance computing infrastructure, including Rosie, the university’s NVIDIA-powered supercomputing cluster. GauthierDickey also holds the Direct Supply Chair of Applied AI and Software Innovation, which is funded through a generous philanthropic gift from Regent Bob and Jenny Hillis and Direct Supply. Prior, GauthierDickey was chair of the Computer Science Department at the University of Denver. During his six-year tenure as chair, he led transformative growth, doubling student enrollment, expanding faculty and launching new programs in cybersecurity, data science and artificial intelligence. His leadership was marked by a strong emphasis on student success, interdisciplinary collaboration and industry engagement. bio: Dr. Alyssa Genschaw is an assistant professor in MSOE's Mathematics Department. Her research combines harmonic analysis, geometric measure theory and partial differential equations to study the parabolic measure corresponding to a divergence form parabolic operator.

name: David Gerow
title: Adjunct Associate Professor
research_summary: Mechanical Design; Mechanical Engineering; Engineering Mechanics
bio: David Gerow is an adjunct associate professor in MSOE's Mechanical Engineering Department. He joined MSOE in 1981 as a lecturer. Gerow earned his bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering from MSOE and his master's degree in engineering mechanics from the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee. He also is the owner of True Wind Engineering in Milwaukee.

name: Ron Gerrits
title: Professor/Program Director
research_summary: Science Education; Guided Inquiry; Physiology
bio: Dr. Ron Gerrits is a professor and the MS Perfusion program director in the Electrical, Computer and Biomedical Engineering department and has been a faculty member at MSOE since 1998. His professional interests are centered around best practices and resource development in science education, mainly in the domain of physiology. As an active member of the Human Anatomy and Physiology Society, he contributed to the creation of a broad set of undergraduate A&P learning outcomes that are now commonly used by textbook publishers. He has contributed to multiple resources for physiology education including the Open Learning Initiative anatomy and physiology course, National Academy Foundation high school physiology project and the TopHat digital anatomy and physiology textbook. In addition, he has authored a set of guided inquiry activities of which selected ones are available in the Jensen et. al. POGIL Activities for Introductory Anatomy and Physiology Courses and through membership at the Human Anatomy and Physiology Society webpage. Service activities include leadership in the Human Anatomy and Physiology Society, where he served as President-Elect, President and Past-President.

name: Richard Gillard
title: Clinical Assistant Professor
research_summary: Nurse Education; Nursing; Extracorporeal Life Support; Critical-Care Nursing
bio: Rich Gillard is a clinical assistant professor in the MSOE School of Nursing. His areas of expertise include adult critical care and trauma critical care. Rich has experience ranging from adult critical care nursing, critical care nursing education at Froedtert Hospital, pediatric/neonatal emergency and transport nursing at Children´s Wisconsin and flight nursing at Flight for Life. Rich has also worked as a paramedic instructor.

name: William Gonwa
title: Professor, Program Director
research_summary: Civil Engineering; Water Resources Engineering; Wastewater Collection; Stormwater Management; Flood Control; Statistics; Infiltration and Inflow
bio: Professor William Gonwa has worked in the fields of wastewater collection, storm water management, and flood protection since 1984. He received his doctorate from Marquette University, his masters from the University of Kentucky, and his bachelors from the University of Wisconsin-Madison, all in civil and environmental engineering. Dr. Gonwa is on the faculty of the Milwaukee School of Engineering (MSOE). He started as a part-time adjunct professor in the Masters of Science in Environmental Engineering Program in 2002. In 2010, he accepted a full-time appointment in the Civil and Architectural Engineering and Construction Management Department. As of the fall of 2019, Dr. Gonwa has been serving as the program director for the Civil Engineering degree. Prior to 2010, Dr. Gonwa spent 25 years as in consulting engineering at CH2M Hill, Crispell-Snyder Consulting Engineers, Symbiont Science, Engineering, and Construction, including two years volunteering In Panama doing development projects. He is a registered professional engineer in the State of Wisconsin. Dr. Gonwa is fluent in Spanish having lived and worked in Mexico, Panama, and Peru for several years. Dr. Gonwa coordinates foreign learning experiences for department student. He enjoys riding bicycle for pleasure and commuting and plays clarinet in the Wauwatosa Community Band.

name: Douglas Grabenstetter

bio: Dr. Doug Grabenstetter is a member of the industrial engineering faculty in MSOE's Mechanical Engineering Department. He joined the faculty in 2015. Grabenstetter specializes in quality, Design of Experiments and Lean Six Sigma. He has more than 20 years of manufacturing experience in a variety of industries. He was a continuous improvement manager and Master Black Belt at Schneider Electric, and a Six Sigma Master Black Belt with Siemens Energy and Automation Inc.

name: David Grassl

bio: David Grassl is an assistant professor in the Civil and Architectural Engineering and Construction Management Department at MSOE. He has industrial experience as a mechanical engineer, designing and specifying HVAC systems for commercial buildings. David is also the founding principal of Dynamic Consulting Engineering LLC, a consulting engineering firm he manages in addition to his teaching duties.

name: Kevin Hart
title: Associate Professor
research_summary: Vascular Fiber-Reinforced Composites; Polymeric Materials; Mechanical Engineering; Additive Manufacturing; Multi-Functional Materials
bio: Dr. Kevin Hart is an Associate Professor in MSOE's Mechanical Engineering Department teaching classes in the areas of solid mechanics and composite materials. Dr. Hart is also the coordinator of the Capstone Senior Design sequence for ME Seniors. Dr. Hart earned a Bachelor of Science degree in Engineering Mechanics and Astronautics from the University of Wisconsin-Madison, as well as a Master of Science and Doctor of Philosophy in Aerospace Engineering from the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign. Dr. Hart advises undergraduate students on research projects in areas of self-healing materials, composite materials, and polymer additive manufacturing. Dr. Hart also directs MSOE’s Pep Band (the Sound Engineers) and is the faculty advisor of MSOE’s Chess Club.

name: Robert Hasker
title: Professor
research_summary: Software Engineering Education; Programming Languages; Object Oriented Design
bio: Dr. Robert Hasker is a professor in the Computer Science and Software Engineering Department at MSOE, where he teaches courses at all levels, especially in software engineering. He also has experience teaching at University of Illinois, Hendrix College, and UW-Platteville. In addition to academic experience, Hasker has worked on a number of projects in industry over a broad range of areas including avionics, instrument control, billing, sales support, and source code instrumentation.

name: Eryn Hassemer
title: Associate Professor
research_summary: Cell Biology; Biomolecular Engineering; Molecular Biology
bio: Dr. Eryn Hassemer is an associate professor in Milwaukee School of Engineering’s Physics and Chemistry Department where she primarily teaches courses in the biomolecular engineering program. She earned her Ph.D. in cell biology, molecular biology and genetics from Medical College of Wisconsin, and a bachelor’s degree in human biology from UW-Green Bay. She previously taught part-time at Milwaukee School of Engineering, and was a graduate research assistant and laboratory technician at Medical College of Wisconsin.

name: Michael Hayes
title: Assistant Professor
research_summary: Thermal Sciences; Thermochemical Oxidation; Solar Energy; Thermochemical Energy Storage; Mechanical Engineering
bio: Michael Hayes' graduate studies have been primarily focused on the area of thermal science. He has spent three years designing, fabricating, and demonstrating a pair of high-temperature thermochemical reactors that provide a zero-carbon method for stowing and releasing thermal energy. Michael also dedicated a significant portion of his graduate studies to the rewarding topic of undergraduate education. He received a Graduate Teaching Fellowship from the American Society of Mechanical Engineering, one component of which was the opportunity to teach his own section of undergraduate thermodynamics.

name: Amy Heikkinen
title: Clinical Assistant Professor
research_summary: Biology; Perfusion; Kinesiology
bio: Amy Keikkinen is a clinical assistant professor in the M.S. Perfusion program in the (ECBE) Electrical, Computer and Biomedical Engineering department. She has been a faculty member at MSOE since 2022. As a Perfusionist, Amy Heikkinen pumps a variety of adult cardiac cases including, but not limited to: valve replacements, CABGs and OPCABGs, ascending aortic aneurysms/dissections, hemiarch repairs with circulatory arrest and cerebral perfusion, thoracic aneurysm repairs with circulatory arrest, LVAD insertions/change-outs, and heart transplants. She also sits bedside for ECMO patients in the ICU and manages patients in cooperation with CV surgeons and critical care physicians. Furthermore, Amy provides standby assistance during transcatheter aortic valve replacements, lead extractions, chest explorations, etc.

name: Kate Herrmann
title: Clinical Assistant Professor
research_summary: Perfusion; Microsoft Excel; MINITAB; MATLAB; Biomedical Engineering
bio: Katelyn Herrmann is a clinical assistant professor in the M.S. Perfusion program in the (ECBE) Electrical, Computer and Biomedical Engineering department. She has been a faculty member at MSOE since 2019.

name: Dylan Heuer
title: Assistant Professor
research_summary: Mathematics; Combinatorics; Sagemath
bio: Dr. Dylan Heuer is an Assistant Professor for the Mathematics Department at Milwaukee School of Engineering. In 2021, he completed his Ph.D. in mathematics at North Dakota State University. Heuer's research area is in combinatorics and deals with various generalizations of permutations and alternating sign matrices. Learning and using Sagemath has been an integral part of his research. Heuer loves teaching mathematics, and has had the opportunity to teach a wide variety of courses ranging from Intermediate Algebra to Calculus to upper-level Combinatorics.

name: Matt Hietpas
title: Clinical Associate Professor
research_summary: Cardiopulmonary Bypass; Biomedical Engineering; Perfusion; Medical Devices; Medical Informatics
bio: Matthew Hietpas is a clinical assistant professor in the M.S. Perfusion program in the (ECBE) Electrical, Computer and Biomedical Engineering department. He has been a faculty member at MSOE since 1994.

bio: Nick Hirsch is a clinical assistant professor in the M.S. Perfusion program in the (ECBE) Electrical, Computer and Biomedical Engineering department. He has been a faculty member at MSOE since 2025.

name: Rick Hoadley
title: Adjunct Professor
research_summary: Power Quality; Power Electronics; AC Motors; AC Drives; Higher Education; DC Drives; DC Motors; Electrical Engineering; Electrical Machines
bio: Rick Hoadley is an adjunct associate professor in the Electrical, Computer and Biomedical Engineering Department. His areas of specialization include DC drives, AC drives (low voltage, medium voltage), drive applications, DC motors, AC motors, transformers, power distribution, power line harmonics, power quality, product training and Simplorer simulations. In addition to teaching electrical systems courses at MSOE, Hoadley is a principal consulting applications engineer for ABB Inc. He also has industrial experience as a technical program manager with Rockwell Automation, and as a program manager for Warner Electric Brake and Clutch, SECO div. of DANA Corp. and Borg-Warner Power Electronics.

name: Sue Hoerchner
title: Adjunct Assistant Professor
research_summary: Program Management; Performance Management; Leadership Development; Marketing; Higher Education; Talent Management; Change Management; Corporate Communications
bio: Sue Hoerchner joined MSOE in 1988 as continuing education coordinator. Although a marketing major, she quickly developed an interest in hydraulics and mechanical engineering due to her role in promoting the Fluid Power Institute’s courses to the public. Through her years of service at MSOE, Hoerchner has applied her passion for continual learning and career development to expand her role in a variety of areas in Enrollment Management, the Applied Technology Center, and as an adjunct faculty member in the Humanities, Social Science and Communication Department and Rader School of Business. Hoerchner’s career interests led her to pursue opportunities outside of higher education where she has gained experience in marketing, sales and human resources management. The common thread through her career is her enthusiasm for growth and development of people. Through opportunities at BORN Information Services, Clifton Gunderson LLP, and Kohl’s Corporation, she has been able to align her professional interests to strategies for talent development and most recently shared services delivery. In addition, she is able to bring real-world examples to the classroom as an MSOE adjunct faculty member.

name: Steve Holland
title: Professor, Program Director, Vice Chair
research_summary: Antennas; Electromagnetics; RF/Microwave Engineering; Analog Electronics; Engineering Education
bio: Dr. Steve Holland is a professor, the department vice-chair, and the electrical engineering program director in the Electrical, Computer and Biomedical Engineering department and has been a faculty member at MSOE since 2013. He serves as program director for the Electrical Engineering program. His specialties include RF/microwave engineering, antennas, electromagnetics, analog circuit design, and engineering education. Before joining the faculty at MSOE, Holland worked as a senior sensors engineer for MITRE Corp. and as a microwave engineer for the Medical College of Wisconsin.

name: Jon Howard
title: Clinical Assistant Professor
research_summary: Higher Education; Computer Science; Electrical Engineering; Clinical Perfusion
bio: Jonathan Howard is a clinical assistant professor in the M.S. Perfusion program in the (ECBE) Electrical, Computer and Biomedical Engineering department. He has been a faculty member at MSOE since 2011. After graduating from MSOE's biomedical engineering program, Jon continued his education to become a perfusionist. He is currently a staff perfusionist with Aurora Medical Group and chairs the Perfusion Simulation Committee at MSOE.

name: David Howell
title: Professor
research_summary: American Literature; At-Risk Education; Technical Communication; Ethics; Creative Thinking; Research Methods; Postmodern Pedagogical Theory
bio: Dr. David Howell is a professor in the Humanities, Social Science, and Communication Department at MSOE. He has held positions at MSOE including Associate Director for Faculty Development, Dean of Students, Chair for Servant-Leadership, and Program Director. He teaches courses in ethics, creative thinking, composition, and research methods, and has created courses in Creative Non-fiction and Eastern Philosophy. He received a bachelor's degree in English from Whitworth College, an M.F.A. in creative writing from the University of Alaska Fairbanks, and an interdisciplinary Ph.D. from Washington State University. Prior to joining MSOE in 2003, he worked in the high-tech sector as a project manager and instructional designer for companies such as Microsoft, Lindsay Communication, The Write Stuff, and Pointshare Corporation.

name: Scott Hrdlicka
title: Adjunct Assistant Professor
research_summary: Search Engine Marketing; Digital Marketing Functions; Market Planning; Marketing; Brand Development; Marketing Management; SEO
bio: Dr. Scott Hrdlicka is an Adjunct Assistant Professor in MSOE's Rader School of Business. He is a dynamic thought leader and leverages expertise in marketing, digital strategy, digital transformation, omnichannel, business development, brand development, brand strategy, major relationship cultivation, team leadership, needs assessment, training/presentation, solution implementation, strategic reporting, and communications to support key initiatives and profitability. Hrdlicka currently serves as the Director of Integrated Marketing and Brand Strategy for The Heico Companies, one of the largest private equity holding companies in the United States.

bio: Dr. Paul Hudec is an associate professor in MSOE's Rader School of Business. He primarily teaches courses in knowledge management, leadership and management principles, strategic management, economics, information systems, ethics, business and government relations, health care economics, and non-profit leadership. Prior to joining academia he gained industrial experience as a cost accounting supervisor for In-Sink-Erator, as CFO/CIO/COO of Saint Francis Seminary, and as controller/CIO of the Pettit National Ice Center.

name: Olga Imas
title: Professor, Director of Applied AI Education
research_summary: Molecular Imaging; Medical Imaging; EEG Analysis; Digital Signal Processing; Computing Tomography; Biomedical Engineering; Signal Processing
bio: Dr. Olga Imas is a Professor in the Electrical, Computer and Biomedical Engineering department and has been a faculty member at MSOE since 2008. She teaches a variety of courses in biomedical digital signal processing, signals and systems analysis, medical imaging, computing in biomedical engineering, and circuit theory. She is a founder/CEO of iBioTekk, LLC. consulting group. Imas acts as an expert consultant for algorithm and product development with emphasis on neurodiagnostic EEG and advanced imaging applications for neurology, cardiology, and oncology. Her technical areas of expertise include signal and image processing, deep learning, and statistical analysis. Imas has over 20 peer-reviewed publications and five patents. Her professional interests include traumatic brain injury, stroke and ischemic disease, physiological mechanisms of Alzheimer’s disease, and anesthesia monitoring. Prior to joining the faculty at MSOE, Imas was a product manager for MICT Neurology Applications at GE Healthcare.

bio: Jennifer Jablonowski is an experienced dual-certified Primary Care Pediatric & Family Nurse Practitioner, with current APNP and DEA registrations. Jennifer completed her Post-Master’s Certificate Program to obtain certification as a Family Nurse Practitioner in 2018.

bio: Troy Jacoby is a lecturer in MSOE's Civil and Architectural Engineering and Construction Management Department. His industrial experience includes work as a senior design architect associate wtih Eppstein Uhen Architects.

bio: Dr. Timothy Johnson is an Adjunct Associate Professor in the Electrical, Computer and Biomedical Engineering department and has been a faculty member at MSOE since 2016. Prior to joining the academic ranks, Dr. Johnson enjoyed a thirty year career in the advanced technology industry spanning the military, industrial, commercial and consumer markets. He was involved in basic and applied research, product development, engineering management, and business management. He has designed or been responsible for the design of over 250 integrated circuits and was responsible for more than $2B of integrated circuits on an annual basis. He worked for Motorola, Harris Corporation, IBM and RCA and indirectly with every major semiconductor company around the world.

bio: Dr. Tabia Jones is an adjunct assistant professor in the MBA in Education Leadership program in MSOE's Rader School of Business. Jones is CEO and president of St. Joseph Academy. She has more than 20 years of experience in the education field, most recently as chief of schools for Universal Companies. Jones has also served as the executive director of curriculum, instruction and pupil services for Shorewood School District, director of instruction for Waukesha School District and principal in the Menomonee Falls School District.

name: Patrick Jung
title: Professor
research_summary: American History; German Art History; Cultural Anthropology; American Indian History
bio: Dr. Patrick Jung is a professor in MSOE's Humanities, Social Science, and Communication Department. He is a historian who also teaches courses in art history and cultural anthropology. Jung joined MSOE in 2003, and his history courses include modern European history and the history of World War II; topics in American history, such as the American Revolution and the Civil War; and the history of Mesoamerica, particularly the ancient Maya and Aztecs. He has also taught European art history and German art history. He teaches several cultural anthropology courses, including a general survey course on cultural anthropology; American Indian cultures; and the anthropology of religion, magic, and witchcraft. Dr. Jung believes international travel can be a powerful pedagogical tool in undergraduate education. From 2013 to 2023, he led trips to Munich and Vienna for students interested in seeing major works of European and German art in both cities. He has also traveled extensively in Central America with students engaged in service work in under-resourced rural communities. On these service trips, students build water projects, provide microfinance, and bring medical services to under-resourced rural communities. These trips led him to join a research team examining students' pedagogical preparation for international service-learning experiences. Dr. Jung has authored books and articles on various topics concerning American history (particularly American Indian history) and German art

name: Richard Jungmann
title: Instructor
research_summary: Mechanical Components; Finite Element Analysis; Mechanical Engineering; Simulations; Standby Generators
bio: Dr. Richard Jungmann is an adjunct associate professor in MSOE's Mechanical Engineering Department. He teaches courses in both the undergraduate and graduate programs, including Statics, Dynamics, Applied Strength of Materials, Mechanical Components, Mechanisms, Mechanics, Finite Element, Mechanics of Materials, Advanced Mechanics and Advanced Mechanical Systems Design. His more than 30 years of practical experience in product design and R&D allows him to connect the course material to real world applications. He is a capstone advisor for both undergraduate and graduate students' final projects, and serves on MSOE's Mechanical Engineering Advisory Committee.

Perfusion program in the (ECBE) Electrical, Computer and Biomedical Engineering department. She has been a faculty member at MSOE since 2009. Kirsten is currently a Certified Clinical Perfusionist for the Medical College of Wisconsin and Advocate Aurora Healthcare. Previously she held a similar role with Children's Hospital of Wisconsin and Wisconsin Heart Group, SC.

name: Sudhir Kaul
title: Department Chair, Professor
research_summary: Passive Vibration Isolation; Motorcycle Dynamics; Structural Dynamics and Control; Fracture Mechanics and Diagnostics
bio: Dr. Sudhir Kaul is chair of Mechanical Engineering Department at MSOE where he oversees the strategic direction and academic development of the department. He works closely with faculty members to enhance the curriculum, strengthen industry partnerships, and promote collaborative research initiatives. Kaul came to MSOE from Western Carolina University in North Carolina where he served as a professor in WCU’s School of Engineering and Technology and program director of the school’s engineering program. He began his academic career as a senior lecturer at the University of Pretoria in South Africa and then moved to the University of Mount Union in Ohio where he served as an assistant professor and interim department chair. Kaul has held academic positions since 2008. Kaul’s industry experiences include development of vibration isolation systems, motorcycle powertrains, and hydraulic systems. Additionally, he has published more than 75 articles in peer-reviewed journals and conference proceedings on topics such as dynamic modeling for vibration isolation, motorcycle dynamics, and fracture diagnostics. He authored “Modeling and Analysis of Passive Vibration Isolation Systems,” a reference book for engineers and researchers involved in the design, development, modeling, analysis, and testing of passive vibration isolation systems and as a reference for a graduate course in vibration modeling and analysis. research_summary: Nursing Education; Psychology; Nursing
bio: Sara Keen is interested in education and preparing the next generation of nurses. During her academic career, Keen has been recognized often by her peers as a leader. She also has served on the statewide curriculum committee, working on curriculum revisions that have been implemented at 16 colleges.

name: Elizabeth Kelley
title: Assistant Professor
research_summary: Mathematics; Cluster Algebras‎; Algebraic Combinatorics‎; Discrete Mathematics; Abstract Algebra
bio: Elizabeth Kelley, Ph.D., is an assistant professor in the Mathematics Department at Milwaukee School of Engineering. Her research focuses on algebraic combinatorics, particularly cluster algebras and related generalizations. Her work examines combinatorial and algebraic structures including generalized cluster algebras, graph LP algebras, cluster scattering diagrams, theta functions and combinatorial models associated with orbifolds and punctured surfaces. Her research has appeared in journals and conference proceedings in algebraic and enumerative combinatorics. Kelley previously served as a postdoctoral research associate and lecturer at the University of Oklahoma and as a Combinatorics RTG postdoctoral fellow at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. She has also contributed to mathematical seminars, conferences and undergraduate research mentoring. She earned a Ph.D. in mathematics from the University of Minnesota in 2021, where she worked under the supervision of Gregg Musiker. She earned a Bachelor of Science in mathematics, with a minor in Arabic, from Harvey Mudd College.

name: John Kellogg

research_summary: Wisconsin History; German Language; Media Studies; Applied Linguistics; Second Language Acquisition; Linguistic Typology; Cultural Studies; Irish Language
bio: John Kellogg is a lecturer in the Humanities, Social Science, and Communication Department at MSOE. He earned his bachelor's degree in German studies from the University of Wisconsin-Parkside and his master's degree in foreign language and literature from the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee. He is in the process of obtaining his Ph.D. in linguistics from the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee. He joined MSOE in 2014 and teaches German and linguistics courses. Prior to joining MSOE, he taught courses at the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee and was a director at the Goethe House Wisconsin.

name: Richard Kelnhofer
title: Associate Professor
research_summary: Power Electronics; Data Center Design; Telecommunication Systems; Electrical Engineering
bio: Dr. Rich Kelnhofer is an Associate Professor in the Electrical, Computer and Biomedical Engineering department and has been a faculty member at MSOE since 2008. Dr. Kelnhofer is an expert in the areas of power electronics, datacenter design, electrical engineering and higher education pedagogy. Prior to joining MSOE, Dr. Kelnhofer gained industrial experience in the telecommunications sector at Norlight Telecommunications and KDL working in numerous technical and management areas. He and his teams were responsible for the design of a multistate fiber optic network along with the daily operations, monitoring and support of the network. Dr. Kelnhofer also was responsible in the design and operation of Norlight and KDL's datacenters. At MSOE, Dr. Kelnhofer led the Electrical Engineering Techonolgy and Electrical Engineering programs as Program Director from 2008-2012 and 2012-2019, respectively.

bio: Kate Kerrigan is a lecturer for the Mechanical Engineering Department and an adjunct trainer in MSOE's Rader School of Business. She is a reliability and operations excellence engineer with expertise in management, maintenance and reliability Management; RCM & FMEA; lean manufacturing; project management; operations, and coaching. She helps companies focus on process in order to maximize their assets and results.

bio: Md Khorrom Khan holds a Ph.D. in Computer Science and Engineering (CSE) and has over 5 years of industry experience as a Software Quality Assurance Engineer. During his doctoral studies at the University of North Texas (UNT), Khan worked as a teaching assistant and actively engaged in teaching a range of graduate and undergraduate courses, including Computer Science I, Computer Science II, Software Engineering, and Usability Testing. In addition to his TA role, Khan also served as an instructor for multiple summer camps and provided mentorship in the NSF-funded Research Experience for Undergraduates (REU) program. His commitment and effective teaching approach were recognized with the prestigious “Outstanding Teaching Assistant Award” from the Department of CSE. During Khan's tenure as a graduate student at UNT, he worked under the mentorship of Dr. Renee Bryce at the Research Innovation in Software Engineering (RISE) lab, focusing on innovative Android Graphical User Interface (GUI) testing techniques using reinforcement learning algorithms and novel Test Case Prioritization techniques for Android GUI test suites. The department of CSE at UNT recognized Khan's academic excellence with the “Outstanding Doctoral Student Award”. Additionally, Khan has held leadership positions in several student organizations as a president, such as World Echoes, Bangladesh Student Association, and Association for Computing Machinery at UNT. Lal is a major in the United States Army Reserve and has served in a combat support hospital. She teaches combat medics, pre-hospital trauma life support, and combat life saver classes.

bio: Dr. Jeff LaMack is a professor and the biomedical engineering program director in the Electrical, Computer and Biomedical Engineering department and has been a faculty member at MSOE since 2006. He teaches on topics such as biological transport phenomena, biomaterials, computer programming, biostatistics, and biomedical engineering design. Dr. LaMack's research interests lie in teaching methodologies in undergraduate biomedical engineering courses, fluid mechanics of blood flow in arteries, endothelial cell biology, pathology of atherosclerosis, and use of 3D modeling and imaging of blood flow patterns to inform clinical interventions. Most recently, Dr. LaMack has engaged in consulting projects involving artificial intelligence applications in medical devices and diagnostic systems.

name: Devon Lantagne

bio: Devon Lantagne is an assistant professor in the Electrical, Computer and Biomedical Engineering department and has been a faculty member at MSOE since 2023. He is a dedicated educator and lifelong learner with 8+ years of teaching experience in embedded systems and biomedical instrumentation. His research has focused on human motor control and the use of subconscious memories to guide future movements. He has developed expertise in low-level embedded systems, data processing in MATLAB, state machines, biomedical device design, signal processing, and linear and nonlinear modeling.

name: Amii LaPointe

bio: Amii LaPointe is an adjunct assistant professor in the Humanities, Social Science, and Communication Department at MSOE. She earned her associate degree in science from Skagit Valley College, her bachelor's degree in technical communication from the University of Washington, and her master's in technical communication management from Mercer University. She teaches user experience courses including Digital Portfolio, Creative Thinking, and Agile Project Management. She also teaches at Waukesha County Technical College. She has industry experience working for Northwestern Mutual as the director of user experience. She also serves on MSOE's Diversity Committee and User Experience and Communication Design Industrial Advisory Committee.

Lee is also part of a team of faculty and students working on a National Science Foundation I-Corp funded research project titled “Developing an Artificial Red-Blood-Cell Product.” He also has been involved with the Clinical and Translational Science Institute of Southeast Wisconsin (CTSI), and the MSOE Center for BioMolecular Modeling. He will be serving as the Milwaukee section chair of the American Chemical Society in 2021.

name: DeAnna Leitzke
title: Department Chair, Professor
research_summary: Higher Education; Servant Leadership; Construction Management; Project-Based Experiential Learning
bio: Dr. DeAnna Leitzke serves as chair of the Civil and Architectural Engineering and Construction Management Department at Milwaukee School of Engineering. Leitzke earned her undergraduate degree in architectural engineering from MSOE and went on to earn her M.S. in Engineering Management from MSOE. She holds a Ph.D. in Leadership for the Advancement of Learning and Service in Higher Education from Cardinal Stritch University. Prior to serving as associate vice president of academic excellence, she founded the CREATE Institute at MSOE in 2018, taught as an associate professor in MSOE’s Civil and Architectural Engineering and Construction Management Department, and was the Pieper Family Endowed Chair for Servant-Leadership. Leitzke has industrial experience as an architectural engineer with Reserve Advisors Inc. and as an architectural engineer with Affiliated Engineers. As a lifelong resident of Milwaukee County, Leitzke is dedicated to serving the community. She is a board member of SHARP Literacy Inc., program quality committee member of the Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Milwaukee, and committee member of the Wisconsin Servant-Leader Group. awards.abstract: This project will contribute to the national need for well-educated scientists, mathematicians, engineers, and technicians by supporting the retention and graduation of high-achieving, low-income students with demonstrated financial need at the Milwaukee School of Engineering, an urban private, non-profit university. Over its five-year duration, the project will fund scholarships to fifteen unique full-time students who are pursuing bachelor’s degrees in Mechanical Engineering. Scholars will be selected in two cohorts of first year mechanical engineering students. The Scholars will be retained and assisted through degree completion and placement into the workforce or graduate school. In addition to scholarships, the program will provide Scholars with a robust suite of support structures that include social activities, peer tutoring, shadowing experiences, student-faculty interaction, car…

Her research focuses on Latin American literature and visual culture, with a specialization in the Southern Cone. Her current book project, War, Photography, and Visual Citizens: Territorial and Visual Expansion in the Construction of Chile and Argentina, spotlights the role and impact of photographers within an expanded public sphere and growing state power. bio: Sarah Marquis, Ph.D., is an adjunct assistant professor in the Mathematics Department at Milwaukee School of Engineering, where she teaches probability and statistics. She holds a doctorate in statistics and applied probability from the University of California, Santa Barbara. Her academic work focuses on statistical methods for clustered and longitudinal data, with particular attention to binary outcomes, repeated measures and psychometric analysis. Her doctoral research examined cluster-robust variance estimators for binary observations in heterogeneous groups and their application to psychometric analyses of repeated measures. Marquis’s research incorporates classical test theory, item response theory, Rasch measurement and generalized estimating equations. Her dissertation developed and evaluated bias-adjusted methods for improving statistical inference in highly heterogeneous and unbalanced clustered settings. Before joining Milwaukee School of Engineering, Marquis served as a teaching associate and teaching assistant at UC Santa Barbara and worked as a researcher with Modus Outcomes.
