awards.abstract: Title: Understanding the Role of Computational Thinking in Engineering Education Abstract: The need for undergraduate engineering students to learn computing has dramatically increased as computing has become more important in engineering practice. Many engineering colleges have responded to this change by requiring their engineering students to take computing classes. Some of these classes are now central to the first year of college engineering education. Computing classes are considered to be extremely difficult by many students, especially those who have not been exposed to computing in high school. Inequities in the K-12 education system mean that some students often have less opportunity to be exposed to computing before college than others. As a result, integrating computing into engineering education may exacerbate existing inequities in engineering education and reduce diversity…

bio: Dr. Meier is the undergraduate Computer Engineering Program Director and a professor in the ECBE Department. His computer engineering specialty is Computer Architecture. He is a member of IEEE, IEEE-HKN, and the IEEE Computer, Education, and Professional Communications societies. He joined IEEE as a student and has an extensive history of membership and service. He also has a professional service record as a member of the American Society for Engineering Education (ASEE) and its Educational Research and Methods Division (ERM), Electrical and Computer Engineering Division (ECE), and First-Year Engineering Education Division (FYE). Dr. Meier grew up on a farm on a Sioux Indian reservation in Nebraska. Agricultural machines fascinated him. He loved examining and fixing tractor engines, augers, combines, automatic livestock feeders, and other equipment. He liked solving problems using tools and determination. While in high school, the personal computer era dawned and fantastic new machines running software changed the world. These machines used ceramic chips and electricity to do cool things! The Apple II and TI-99/4a were simple compared to modern computers, but they became his platforms to explore automation and control using the BASIC and Pascal programming languages. He quickly discovered his passion for computing and enjoyed helping his classmates learn about how computer hardware and software work. By the end of high school, it was clear that a professional career in engine

bio: Hosam Olimat, Ph.D., is an assistant professor in the Department of Civil and Architectural Engineering and Construction Management at the Milwaukee School of Engineering. His work focuses on construction safety, off-site construction, facility management and data-driven methods for improving construction decision-making. Olimat’s research examines safety performance across construction activities and develops evaluation frameworks that incorporate leading and lagging indicators. His work has addressed workers’ compensation decision support, safety modification metrics, construction risk factors and the limitations of traditional experience modification ratings. His research also explores emerging technologies in the built environment, including blockchain, building information modeling, the Internet of Things, digital twins and artificial intelligence. These technologies are studied as tools for strengthening information management, transparency, monitoring and operational decision-making in construction and facilities management. Olimat earned a Doctor of Philosophy in civil and construction engineering and a Master of Science in engineering with a civil engineering concentration from Western Michigan University. His publications have appeared in journals including Buildings, the Journal of Construction Engineering and Management and the Journal of Management in Engineering.

bio: Alexander Pezewski has a master’s degree and over 25 years of professional experience as a software developer, project manager, business analyst, development team manager, and IT director in a variety of different industries. Pezewski teaches topics stuch as robotics, cyber security, artificial intelligence, data mining, data structures and algorithms, computer architecture, and programming languages such as Java, Python, and C#.

bio: Brian Pfeifer is a lecturer in MSOE's Civil and Architectural Engineering and Construction Management Department. He has global industry experience as a Director of Operations for Johnson Controls, focusing on building automation, fire, security and energy management systems.

bio: Cory Powers is a lecturer in MSOE's Civil and Architectural Engineering and Construction Management Department. He is a principal with HGA. and a mechanical designer specializing in plumbing, medical gas, and fire protection systems for health care, education, public and corporate facilities. Powers focuses on sustainable outcomes, researching and analyzing available and new technologies that provide energy-efficient, long-lasting and cost-effective solutions.

His areas of focus include statistical signal processing, computational structural biology, adaptive array processing, and radar systems. He spent three years as a technical staff member at the MIT Lincoln Laboratory working on cutting edge technology, allowing him to bring real-world experience into the classroom.

Raut has been active as a collaborator for the Gravity Research Institute and is a longtime member of the Scientist's Pool, Council for Scientific and Industrial Research.

bio: Dr. Tammy Rice-Bailey began her career as a technical writer after graduating from the University of Wisconsin-Parkside with a communication degree. Ten years later, she earned her master’s degree in English literature from DePaul University, and then taught part-time at the College of DuPage in Glen Ellyn, Illinois. At the same time, she became manager of corporate documentation and training departments for several Fortune 500 companies, such as McDonald’s Corporation, Kemper Financial Services and Install Shield Software. She earned her Ph.D. in professional writing from the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee in 2014. Rice-Bailey teaches courses including Freshman Studies, Foundations of Communication Design, Collaborative Design, UX and Com Design Internship, Instructional Design, Interpersonal Communication, and American Literature.

bio: Dr. Derek Riley joined the MSOE faculty in 2016 and is a Professor in the Diercks School of Advanced Computing. He is also program director of MSOE’s Bachelor of Science in Computer Science program, which has a focus in artificial intelligence. In addition to teaching at MSOE, Riley provides consulting services and expert witness services related to Large Language Models, deep learning, facial recognition, computational modeling, high-performance computing, and other related fields. His areas of expertise include deep learning, computer vision, Large Language Models, process modeling and simulation, Scrum, and mobile computing. He is an NVIDIA DLI Certified Instructor.

He teaches Computer Applications in Engineering I, Mechanics of Materials II, Finite Element Methods, Medical Applications in Mechanical Engineering, and advises Senior Design. He earned his bachelor's, master's and doctorate degrees in mechanical engineering from Illinois Institute of Technology. He has additional teaching experience at Tri-State University and North Dakota State University.

bio: Dr. Luis Rodriguez is an assistant professor in MSOE's Mechanical Engineering Department. He teaches Intro to Engineering Design, Engineering Dynamics, Instrumentation, Mechanics III, Automatic Control Systems, and advises Senior Design. He earned his bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering from the University of California, San Diego, his master's in mechanical engineering from the University of Wisconsin-Madison, and his Ph.D. in mechanical engineering from the University of California-Irvine. He is a member of the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) Control Systems Society, IEEE Robotics and Automation Society, American Society for Engineering Education (ASEE), and the Society for the Advancement of Chicanos and Native American Indians in Science (SACNAS).

bio: Megan Roethle is a clinical assistant professor in the M.S. Perfusion program in the (ECBE) Electrical, Computer and Biomedical Engineering department. She has been a faculty member at MSOE since 2019.

name: David Rollins
title: Assistant Professor
research_summary: Marketing; Management; Supply Chains; Business; Business Administration
bio: David Rollins brings a variety of experience to his position as an Assistant Professor in Operations and Systems Management (OSM) in the Rader School of Business. His experience spans the functional areas of information technology, project management, supply chain management, and continuous improvement. He has over 10 years of experience in information technology including server administration, network administration, and programming. He also brings over 14 years of experience in the supply chain and operations management in the industries of papermaking, food packaging, and architectural door manufacturing. His project management experience includes managing IT projects as well as Lean continuous improvement projects.

name: Sheila Ross
title: Depart Chair, Professor, Aso VP Academic Retention
bio: Dr. Sheila Ross is chair of the Electrical, Computer and Biomedical Engineering Department and has been a faculty member at MSOE since 2008. Her current area of research involves the integration of best practices for inclusion and success into the electrical engineering curriculum. Dr. Ross developed a workshop series on Universal Design for Learning (UDL), which supports learners with a wide variety of challenges, including those due to neurological differences such as ASD and ADHD, as well as a wide variety of other challenges faced by students such as stereotype threat, differences in pre-college experiences, and diverse learning and communication styles. She serves on university committees creating policy and recommendations, advises her SWE Collegiate chapter, shares research on diversity with other engineering faculty, and participates in outreach to K-12 schools. She received the “Making a Difference for Women at MSOE” award in recognition of her institutional contributions. She has been active WEPAN, serving as President, Director, and Conference Chair for the WEPAN Change Leader Forum.

name: Darrin Rothe
title: Associate Professor
research_summary: Engineering Education; Electrical Engineering; Bioengineering; Bio Technology
bio: Dr. Darrin Rothe is an associate professor in the Electrical, Computer and Biomedical Engineering department and has been a faculty member at MSOE since 2002. He gained industrial experience as a consulting engineer for Der Tech LLC, a manufacturing engineer for Marquette Medical Systems, and a senior test engineer with Allen-Bradley Company before joining the faculty at MSOE. His areas of expertise include data collection and processing, embedded systems, and programmable logic device applications.

He earned his bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering from the University of Toledo and his master's degree in mechanical engineering from Ohio State University. He gained industry experience working at Stryker-Surgical Instruments, Battelle Memorial Institute-Medical Device Solutions, Synthes-Orthopaedic Medical Devices, and Ethicon Endo-Surgery.

name: Carol Sabel
title: Department Chair, Professor
research_summary: Patient Education; Patient Safety; Nursing Education; Interprofessional Collaboration; Nursing
bio: Dr. Carol Sabel is a professor and chair of the Milwaukee School of Engineering's School of Nursing. She has 30 combined years of experience in nursing, education and research, having cared for patients in obstetrics and same-day surgery settings before focusing on teaching. Dr. Sabel is involved in several local and national nursing organizations, including the Southeast Wisconsin Nursing Alliance, Mental Health Nurse Educators Coalition, National League for Nursing, Wisconsin Nurses Association, American Nurses Association, and the Building Bridges to Advance Nursing Research Conference planning committee. She also served as president of the Delta Gamma At-Large Chapter of Sigma Theta Tau International nursing honor society. Dr. Sabel currently serves on the Wisconsin House planning Sub-committee for the 2022 INACSL Conference. In the School of Nursing. In the School of Nursing, she has been instrumental in developing a partnership with Rogers Behavioral Health and the addition of a Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner track in the MSN program.

name: Joshua Sanders
title: Adjunct Assistant Professor
research_summary: Operational Management; Cybersecurity
bio: With 20 years of experience in various technology and cybersecurity leadership roles, Josh is dedicated to fostering the next generation of cybersecurity professionals as an Adjunct Assistant Professor at the Milwaukee School of Engineering (MSOE). Within the Department of Computer Science and Software Engineering, he contributes to the Cybersecurity minor program, sharing his real-world experience and knowledge with his students. In addition to his role at MSOE, Josh is a Vice President of Information Systems at Heartland Advisors, where he is passionate about safeguarding his organization and their stakeholders from cybersecurity threats. Josh also plays an active role in the cybersecurity community as a member of the Board of Directors for the Milwaukee Chapter of the Information Systems Security Association. His involvement extends to being an active member of FBI InfraGard and the Wisconsin Cyber Threat Response Alliance, where he collaborates with professionals across government, private sector, and higher education to share knowledge, cyber intelligence, and resources. Josh holds a Bachelor's degree in IT Security, a Master's degree in Information Systems, and is CISSP and Security+ certified. When Josh is not safeguarding digital landscapes or shaping future cybersecurity experts, he treasures spending time with his wife and young son. He is also an outdoor enthusiast and enjoys working on ham radio and software-defined radio projects, blending his technical expertise

name: Salah Sarhat
title: Associate Professor
research_summary: Structural Engineering; Natural Building Materials; Green Concrete; Reinforced Masonry; Ultra-High-Performance Concrete; Carbon-Sequestering; Building Science
bio: Dr. Salah Sarhat is an expert educator and researcher with more than two decades of teaching, research, and industry experience. Sarhat is dedicated to world-class education. His teaching style combines solid theoretical knowledge with hands-on experience. He lived and taught in different countries, developing a broad international and cultural understanding that enables him to work and collaborate within a diverse, multicultural contemporary society. Sarhat has extensive experience teaching engineering mechanics, building materials, mechanics of solids, structural analysis, reinforced concrete design, masonry, wood, and steel structures, design of foundations, construction management, and building science. Sarhat's research interests lie at the intersection of structures and materials. He has considerable research and industry experience in sustainable structural and materials engineering, reinforced concrete and masonry, structural fire design, building science, and design and rehabilitation of bridges.

name: Ahmed Sayed
title: Associate Professor
research_summary: Biomechanics; Biomedical Instrumentation; Forensics Biomedical Engineering; Medical Image Processing and Segmentation; Ultrasound Elastography; Tumor Diagnosis
bio: Dr. Sayed is an associate professor in the Electrical, Computer and Biomedical Engineering department and has been a faculty member at MSOE since 2019. From 2017 to 2019, he served as a postdoctoral associate at the Bascom Palmer Eye Institute, University of Miami. He earned his Ph.D. in Mechanical Engineering from West Virginia University in 2013 and his M.S. and B.S. degrees in Systems and Biomedical Engineering from Cairo University in 2008 and 2003, respectively. From 2013 to 2017, he worked at various healthcare facilities as a Medical Technology Consultant and also served as a lecturer in Biomedical Engineering at multiple universities. He is the author/ co-author of over 45 publications in international peer-reviewed journals and conferences and co-inventor of 9 U.S. patents. Additionally, he serves as an expert witness in legal cases involving medical devices and as an expert reviewer for several top-tier journals, including Elsevier Ultrasonics, IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Engineering, IEEE Transactions on Ultrasonics, Ferroelectrics, and Frequency Control, and Ophthalmology. His current research interests include bioinstrumentation applications, diagnosis of tumors using biomechanical models and machine learning algorithms, as well as the development of new digital visual aids for patients with peripheral visual defects.

name: Matt Schaefer
title: Associate Professor
research_summary: Stem; Materials
bio: Dr. Matt Schaefer is an associate professor in the Mechanical Engineering Department at MSOE. He teaches Instrumentation and Control of Systems, Intro to Engineering Design, Materials Science, Engineering Materials, Instrumentation, and advises Senior Design. Prior to joining MSOE in 2005, he taught at the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee and Marquette University. He also gained industry experience at Briggs & Stratton and General Electric Co. He was awarded the 2016 Outstanding Junior Faculty Award from the Manufacturing Division of ASEE and the 2017 Faculty Appreciation Award from the MSOE Student-Athlete Advisory Committee. He earned his bachelor's and master's degrees in mechanical engineering from Marquette University and his doctorate in materials science and engineering from Marquette University.

name: Kyle Schilling

bio: Kyle Schilling is a clinical assistant professor in the M.S. Perfusion program in the (ECBE) Electrical, Computer and Biomedical Engineering department. He has been a faculty member at MSOE since 2015.

name: Timothy Schneller
title: Lecturer
research_summary: AI and Business Strategy; Business Partnerships; Entrepreneurial Thinking; Go-To-Market Strategy; Partnership Quality; Trust and Commitement in Organizations; Intrapreneurship; Marketing Channel Theory
bio: Dr. Tim Schneller brings over 30 years of experience in global channel strategy, partner ecosystem development, and industrial market growth. He earned his Doctor of Business Administration from the University of Maryland Global Campus, where his research explored how AI influences trust, commitment, and power in modern business partnerships. He also holds an MBA from Penn State and dual engineering degrees from the University of Virginia. Schneller is the founder of CollabInspire, a research-driven advisory firm focused on partnership strategy, governance, and collaboration in complex ecosystems. He also serves as Visiting Faculty for the AI Startup Program at the Meltwater Entrepreneurial School of Technology (MEST) in Ghana, where he mentors early-stage founders on market definition, value creation, and go-to-market strategy. At MSOE, Schneller will be teaching courses in strategy, marketing, entrepreneurship, and emerging technologies. His teaching approach bridges research and real-world applications, emphasizing how AI and digital systems are reshaping business models, decision-making, and collaborative innovation. Previously, Schneller served as Senior Director of Channel Strategies at Regal Rexnord, where he led a distributor portfolio representing approximately $800M in revenue and aligned partner execution with business objectives. At Xylem, Honeywell, and General Electric, he held senior leadership roles driving global partner programs, leading digital transformati

bio: Ruth Schwartz has served as an instructor of physics at Milwaukee School of Engineering for over 30 years. Schwartz works closely with the STEM office on the annual Opportunities Conference Science Competition and the Department of Energy Regional Science Bowl.

research_summary: Chemistry; Environmental Engineering; Bioremediation; Biocatalysis; Microbiology
bio: Dr. Anne Schwarzkopf teaches chemistry, biochemistry, environmental chemistry, cell biology and genetics, microbiology, and prokaryotic processes courses in the Physics and Chemistry Department at Milwaukee School of Engineering. Her graduate and postdoctoral research focused on the molecular mechanisms of bioremediation, biocatalysis, and plant/nanoparticle interactions.

bio: Dr. Nebojsa Sebastijanovic is an associate professor in the Mechanical Engineering Department at MSOE. He teaches Mechanics, Vehicle Dynamics, Mechanics I - Statistics, Finite Element Methods, and advises Senior Design. He earned his bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering from McNeese State University, and his master's and doctorate degrees in mechanical engineering from the University of California-Santa Barbara. He is a member of the American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME), the American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics (AIAA), the National Society of Professional Engineers (NSPE), and The International Society for Optical Engineering (SPIE).

name: Cassandra Seefeldt
title: Clinical Assistant Professor
research_summary: Cardiopulmonary Health; Cardiothoracic Surgery; Patient Centered Care; Perfusion; Nursing
bio: Cassie Seefeldt is a clinical assistant professor in the M.S. Perfusion program in the (ECBE) Electrical, Computer and Biomedical Engineering department. She has been a faculty member at MSOE since 2023. Cassie is a hardworking professional with 10 years of experience in the medical field providing exceptional, patient centered care. Currently a perfusionist at St. Luke’s Medical Center, Seefeldt is a dedicated and collaborative team member with a passion for providing high quality, safe patient care. Seefeldt is board certified, and has been practicing independently since September of 2022. Seefeldt provides support to the cardiothoracic surgeons on a variety of cases including: CABG, valves, transplants, ECMO, HIPEC, LVAD, and IABP. She is proficient with the terumo system 1 cardiopulmonary bypass machine, Medtronic autologous cell saver, and quest cardioplegia devices as well as a multitude of MCS support devices.

name: Faisal Shaikh
title: Professor, Program Dir, BioMolecular Eng
research_summary: Reaction Engineering; Materials Science; Biomolecular Engineering; Chemical Engineering; Characterization
bio: Dr. Faisal Shaikh is the biomolecular engineering program director in Milwaukee School of Engineering’s Physics and Chemistry Department. He joined the faculty in 2010 and has developed a significant number of the core chemical engineering courses, albeit with a focus on biology. He has championed several of the program’s industry-academia partnerships for senior design projects.

name: Nadya Shalamova
title: Professor, Program Director
research_summary: Applied Learning; Design; User Experience; Technology; Technical Communication
bio: Dr. Nadya Shalamova is a professor in the Humanities, Social Sciences and Communication Department at MSOE and the program director of user experience. She earned her M.A. in teaching English and German as a foreign language from Tomsk State Pedagogical University, and her M.Phil in descriptive linguistics from Mari State University. She worked for several years in the Laboratory of Siberian Indigenous Language at Tomsk Polytechnic University where she conducted linguistic and anthropological research on one of the endangered (now extinct) native Siberian dialects. At the same time, she taught linguistics and ESL to engineering students. In 2001, she received a Carnegie Fellowship that brought her to the United States. That’s when she first learned about technical communication. She decided to pursue her Ph.D. from New Mexico State University where she was heavily involved in the Freshman Integrated Learning Community Project at the College of Engineering. Shalamova joined MSOE in 2008. She teaches UX and humanities courses including Social Science, UX Practicum, Freshman Studies, Linguistics: Study of Language, and Foundations of UX. She is an advisor to MSOE's University Innovation Fellows and is a CREATE Faculty Fellow.

As MSOE's Institutional Review Board (IRB) Administrator, Ms. Shebesta manages day-to-day operations of MSOE's IRB while providing education and oversight for human subjects research at MSOE, responsible conduct of research, and research compliance. Prior to her career in higher education and human research protections programs, she gained industry experience as a financial analyst with Johnson Controls.

bio: Ashley Sheskey, RN is an experienced pediatric nurse, having served in level III NICU environment and as a school nurse.

name: Jaegeon Shin
title: Adjunct Assistant Professor
research_summary: Complex Geometry; Differential Geometry; Algebraic Geometry; Metric Geometry; Higher Education
bio: Jaegeon Shin, Ph.D., is an Adjunct Assistant Professor in the Mathematics Department at Milwaukee School of Engineering. His academic work centers on complex geometry and related areas of modern mathematics. Shin's research interests include the interaction of differential geometry and algebraic geometry, with particular attention to metric geometry on quiver flag varieties. These topics examine geometric structures and relationships arising in advanced mathematical settings.

name: Mark Simmons
title: Clinical Assistant Professor
research_summary: Clinical Perfusion; Perfusion; Biomedical Engineering
bio: Mark Simmons is a clinical assistant professor in the M.S. Perfusion program in the (ECBE) Electrical, Computer and Biomedical Engineering department. Hee has been a faculty member at MSOE since 2003.

name: Edward Sippel
title: Assistant Professor
research_summary: Structural Engineering; Structural Steel; Finite Element Analysis; Nonlinear Analysis & Stability; Civil Engineering
bio: It will take nearly a month for a demolition contractor to take down a turn-of-the-century building, with a history that harkens back to Milwaukee’s booming brewing industry, that started to collapse earlier this week. "So, my first reaction is water must have got in and corroded something over time," said Ed Sippel, a structural engineer and an assistant professor at MSOE. Sippel, who lives nearby, said the collapse is providing some real-time examples and a way to look at the innards of the building’s turn-of-the-century brick construction, and provide an example to his students of what could go wrong.

name: Brian Slaboch
title: Associate Professor
research_summary: Kinematic Synthesis; Reconfigurable Mechanisims; Mechanisms with Variable Topology; Mechanism Design
bio: Dr. Brian Slaboch is an assistant professor in the Mechanical Engineering Department at MSOE. He is passionate about providing the highest quality education to students by integrating best practices from industry and research into the classroom. Dr. Slaboch is the director of the Reconfigurable Mechanisms Research Group. The research team specializes in the development of new reconfigurable mechanism design theory and its application in the manufacturing, healthcare, and space industries. Prior to joining MSOE in 2019, Slaboch was an assistant professor at Middle Tennessee State University where he helped develop a new Mechatronics Engineering program. He also has industry experience working in the Advanced Automation Group at Joy Global Inc. He earned his bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering from the University of Notre Dame, and both his master's and doctorate degrees in mechanical engineering from Marquette University.

name: Ariana Smies
title: Adjunct Assistant Professor
research_summary: Clinical Trials; Host Response; Biomaterials; Wellness Products
bio: Dr. Ariana Smies is an adjunct assistant professor in the Electrical, Computer and Biomedical Engineering department and has been a faculty member at MSOE since 2022. In addition to teaching at MSOE, Dr. Smies is a project engineer in the Advanced Development in Water Technologies group at Kohler Company. She is focused on how to integrate current advancements surrounding wellness into the products you use every day.

name: Cierra Smith
title: Assistant Professor
research_summary: Construction Management; Traffic Operations; Roadway Design; Transportation; Civil Engineering; Traffic Engineering
bio: Cierra Smith is an expert in transportation and traffic design and teaches in the Civil and Architectural Engineering and Construction Management Department at MSOE. She teaches courses in AutoCAD Civil 3D modeling for civil engineering students.

name: Rebecca Sobanski
title: Associate Professor, PMHNP Program Coordinator
research_summary: Nurse Practitioner; Psychiatric and Mental Health Nursing
bio: Rebecca Sobanski is an Associate Professor and Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner Program Coordinator at the Milwaukee School of Engineering. She is a board-certified Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner providing compassionate and comprehensive mental health care, psychiatric evaluation, diagnosis, and medication management to adults. She works with patients who may be struggling with a variety of mental health issues, including depression, bipolar disorder, anxiety, and ADHD.

name: Won Chul Song
title: Associate Professor, Program Director
research_summary: High-Dimensional Analysis; Statistics; R; SAS; Data Analytics; Machine Learning
bio: Dr. Won Chul Song is an associate professor in the Mathematics Department at MSOE. He is the Program Director of the Actuarial Science program. He teaches courses in probability and statistics, calculus, statistics for actuarial science, and predictive analytics. Prior to teaching, he was a research analyst for Korean Management Association Consultants where he designed surveys on customer satisfaction for government-owned corporations, evaluated research models and provided research solutions for corporations.

name: Tony Spence
title: Lecturer
research_summary: Education Leadership; Engineering Management; Business Administration; New Product Management

name: Aaron Spink
title: Associate Professor
research_summary: Knowledge and Reality; Medieval Philosophy; Early Modern Philosophy; Applied Ethics; American Pragmatism
bio: Aaron Spink is an Assistant Professor at the Milwaukee School of Engineering where he teaches 17th century philosophy and ethics. Previously, Aaron has worked at Dartmouth College, Durham University, the Ohio State University, and the Illinois Institute of Technology as a Fay Horton-Sawyier pre-doctoral teaching fellow. Aaron earned his PhD in 2017 from the University of South Florida. His dissertation explored the positive role of scientific experimentation in the philosophy and methodology of René Descartes and some of his early followers. Aaron has published in early modern philosophy and has done extensive translation and editorial work for the upcoming English edition of Descartes' correspondence. Aaron has also recently begun work on a translation of the philosophical writings of Jacqueline, Gilberte, and Blaise Pascal for Hackett Publishing with Roger Ariew and Daniel Collette.

name: Nick Starkey
title: Clinical Assistant Professor
research_summary: Biology; Pediatric Perfusion; Perfusion
bio: Nicholas Starkey is a clinical assistant professor in the M.S. Perfusion program in the (ECBE) Electrical, Computer and Biomedical Engineering department. He has been a faculty member at MSOE since 2021.

name: Natalie Stocke
title: Clinical Assistant Professor
research_summary: Perfusion; Exercise Physiology; Cardiovascular Perfusion; Cardiopulmonary Bypass; Kinesiology
bio: Natalie Stocke is a clinical assistant professor in the M.S. Perfusion program in the (ECBE) Electrical, Computer and Biomedical Engineering department. She has been a faculty member at MSOE since 2022. Natalie has experience in managing cardiopulmonary bypass during congenital cardiac surgery, constructing circuits individualized to patient size and defect, initiating ECMO support using CentriMag and PediMag, and assisting ECMO technicians in troubleshooting and transportation of patients on support.

name: Carrie Striker
title: Clinical Assistant Professor
research_summary: Cardiovascular Perfusion; Pediatric Perfusion; Congenital Perfusion; Cardiopulonary Bypass; Researcher
bio: Dr. Carrie Striker is a clinical assistant professor in the M.S. Perfusion program in the (ECBE) Electrical, Computer and Biomedical Engineering department. She has been a faculty member at MSOE since 2024. She is a Certified Clinical Perfusionist with 20 years’ experience providing services ranging from tertiary pediatric care to tertiary and community adult care. She is practiced in cardiopulmonary bypass techniques for a wide array of surgical procedures and is experienced in Extracorporeal Life Support methods and techniques. Striker is a pediatric and congenital cardiovascular perfusionist at Childrens Wisconsin and formerly was a pediatric and congenital cardiovascular perfusionist at the Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center's Joint Pediatric Heart Care Program with the University of Kentucky. Striker is a published author, researcher, and a dedicated educator committed to providing comprehensive clinical and didactic instruction. She previously served as innovator and program director for the Pediatric and Congenital Cardiovascular Perfusion Fellowship Program at Children’s Mercy Hospital and the corresponding graduate certificate at University of Missouri Kansas City. She has also served on national and hospital committees and supervised graduate students in the development, implementation, and publication of research.

name: Michael Swedish
title: Adjunct Associate Professor
research_summary: Power Generation; Thermodynamics and Public Policy; Thermodynamics; Resource Utilization
bio: Michael Swedish is an associate professor in the Mechanical Engineering Department at MSOE. He teaches Energy Systems Design Project, Fluid Mechanics, Fluid Mechanics II, Principles of Thermodynamics II, and advises Senior Design. Prior to joining MSOE in 1986, he was an instructor at the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee. He gained industry experience working for several companies, including the City of Milwaukee, Wisconsin Electric Power Co., Argonne National Laboratory, Rexnord Inc., Westinghouse Electric Corp., and Giddings and Lewis Corp. He is a registered Professional Engineer (PE) in Wisconsin. He earned his bachelor's and master's degrees from Marquette University.

name: Tom Swiontek
title: Professor Emeritus
research_summary: Biomedical Engineering; Engineering Education; Electrical Engineering
bio: Dr. Tom Swiontek joined MSOE in 1975 and taught classes in the biomedical engineering and electrical engineering areas. Swiontek brought to MSOE his expertise in biomedical engineering, measurement of current density in tissue, magnetic stimulation and effects of current on tissue, as well as industrial experience working for Allis Chalmers Manufacturing. He has written a number of publications, and is a member of the Institute of Electrical and Electronic Engineers and the American Society for Engineering Education.

name: Josh Szmergalski
title: Lecturer
research_summary: Structural Engineering; Project Management; Structural Inspections
bio: Josh Szmergalski is a lecturer in MSOE's Civil and Architectural Engineering and Construction Management Department and works full-time as a senior engineer for CSD Structural Engineers. He teaches principles of structural engineering and strengths of materials courses.

name: Milad Tatari
title: Assistant Professor
research_summary: Sensors and Actuators; Soft Robotics; Soft Materials; Mechanics; Foldable Structures
bio: Milad Tatari's research interests are the design, analysis and fabrication of unique machines and mechanisms to overcome limitations of traditional systems and impact critical domains such as soft robotics, wearable medical devices and manufacturing industries. This area requires a blend of experience and fundamental insights in mechanical and material engineering.

name: Christopher Taylor

He is the Vice Chair of Operations for the ABET Engineering Accreditation Commission and as a team chair for accreditation site visits. Dr. Taylor is a board member for CSAB and STEM Forward.

The corporate experiences included project management, software engineering, and senior and executive management. He has worked closely with System Dynamics consultants trained at MIT to help control the delivery and staffing over-runs for large software projects. He has authored three books and has been an adjunct professor at MSOE since 2005.

bio: Dr. Charles Tritt is an adjunct associate professor in the Electrical, Computer and Biomedical Engineering department and has been a faculty member at MSOE since 1990. He primarily teaches in the biomedical engineering program. He began his career as a staff engineer at Proctor and Gamble. He returned to school for a master’s degree in biomedical engineering and a Ph.D. in chemical engineering. At MSOE he also has served as the interim biomedical engineering program director. He coordinated MSOE’s 2+2 transfer program with Manipal University in India. He is an ABET program visitor and member of the BME Accreditation Activities Committee (AAC). He regularly teaches the BME program’s Thermodynamics & Transport Phenomena and Sensors, Actuators, & Interfaces courses. He is interested in the application of generative AI technology to biomedical engineering problems and medical devices. He also has extensive experience in biomedical applications of mass, heat, and momentum transfer (particularly in mathematical modeling of adsorption, ion exchange and permeation processes).”

bio: Dr. Prabhakar Venkateswaran is an assistant professor in the Mechanical Engineering Department at MSOE. He teaches courses in thermodynamics, fluids mechanics, heat transfer, and gas turbines. He also regularly advises Senior Design projects. Prior to joining MSOE, he taught at Trinity College in Hartford, CT as a Visiting Assistant Professor, as well as at Iowa State University as a Post-Doctoral Scholar. As a Post-Doctoral Scholar he also worked on developing high-power and high-frequency laser systems to obtain spatio-temporally resolved velocity and multi-scalar measurements in turbulent flames. He earned his bachelor's degrees in Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering from the University of Miami, and his Master's and Doctorate in Aerospace Engineering from the Georgia Institute of Technology.

name: Shira Viel
title: Adjunct Associate Professor
research_summary: STEM Student Success‎; Mathematics Research; Mathematics Education; Curriculum Development; Inclusive Assessment‎
bio: Shira Viel, Ph.D., is an Adjunct Associate Professor at Milwaukee School of Engineering. Her professional work focuses on mathematics education, undergraduate instruction and mathematical research. Her education research examines classroom community, student belonging, inclusive assessment and the design of introductory mathematics courses. Her work addresses how course structures and teaching practices influence undergraduate students' experiences in mathematics and statistics. Viel has also contributed to research in algebraic and geometric combinatorics, including work on cluster algebras, generalized splines on graphs, geometric coefficients and algebraic voting theory. Her teaching and curriculum interests include calculus, discrete mathematics and quantitative learning. She earned a Ph.D. in mathematics from North Carolina State University and has held teaching and research roles in higher education. Her professional activities have included mathematics outreach, faculty development, curriculum design and participation in organizations including the Mathematical Association of America, the Special Interest Group on Research in Undergraduate Mathematics Education and the Association for Women in Mathematics.

bio: I'm an assistant professor of physics at Milwaukee School of Engineering (MSOE). I enjoy teaching intro physics, astronomy, and quantum mechanics. I'm an observational cosmologist and my primary research interest is in using galaxy clusters--the most massive objects in the universe--to measure cosmological parameters such as the amount of normal matter, dark matter, and dark energy in our universe. Trained as an optical astronomer (PhD in Physics from Stanford in 2019), most of my work has been in measuring the mass of galaxy clusters using weak gravitational lensing--the deflection of light's path as it passes near a massive object..

awards.title: I-Corps: A Natural Polymer-Based Engineered Red Blood Cell Product
awards.abstract: The broader impact/commercial potential of this I-Corps project addresses many of the concerns people may have with blood donation and transfusion, including ethical and religious reasons, as well as a number of supply chain related issues. According to the America Red Cross, approximately 36,000 units of red blood cells are needed every day in the U.S., which corresponds to a $1.5 billion annual market. Importantly, many of the risks associated with human blood can be mitigated or eliminated with an engineered product. Other issues include cost and availability of human blood and its processing, such as screening for infectious diseases or spot availability in the supply chain due to natural or other disasters. It is possible that an engineered blood product could become widely available throughout the world and be shipped in large quantities as and where needed, addressing significant …

bio: Dr. Wujie Zhang is currently a professor in Milwaukee School of Engineering’s Physics and Chemistry Department. Zhang truly believes the focus should be on each individual student -- strengthening the student experience through interaction, encouragement, and engagement. Zhang has led several projects based on a biomaterial known as pectin that have focused on drug delivery for cancer treatment, 3D printing for tissue engineering, and engineering artificial red blood cells. Moreover, Zhang has advised senior design projects related to the food industry, such as the development of novel American ginseng-based beverages.

In his position as senior design architect, Zimmerman was charged with initiating building projects by generating functional space requirements, establishing space programs, adjacency diagrams, material research and specification and conceptualizing the overall design. He has coordinated multi-disciplinary teams of engineering consultants, set sustainability and performance targets and was responsible for maintaining the integrity of the initial concept through the entire design and construction process. Zimmerman is the author of several of Wisconsin’s most recognizable buildings. He volunteers his time for the community: he has served as design consultant for Milwaukee’s Lincoln Village Main Street Program, led several design charrettes with Community Design Solutions and the Menomonee Valley Partners overseeing implementation of the 2.0 master plan. Zimmerman is dedicated to the architectural profession leading the AIA Milwaukee and AIA Wisconsin. Zimmerman is a nationally recognized leader in the field of sustainable design. His design interest focuses on the ecology of the built environment, particularly building science topics and high-performance buildings.
